subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept the custom yielding glob walker and bootstrap-only hook scheduling as the bounded fix for bootstrap-context event-loop stalls?
rationale: The implementation and proof are strong, but bootstrap file selection, ordering, and hook timing feed compatibility-sensitive prompt and session state that automation should not redefine unilaterally.

options.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
options.body: Accept the internal scheduling and glob-resolution tradeoff, rebase onto current main, and land after the exact head passes relevant checks.

options.title: Require Live Channel Proof
options.body: Keep the implementation but require one current-head embedded-run with active channel traffic demonstrating that channel I/O remains responsive during bootstrap.

options.title: Pause For Broader Architecture
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers prefer worker isolation, priority scheduling, or caching rather than owning a custom traversal implementation.

recommendation.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
recommendation.body: Accept the internal scheduling and glob-resolution tradeoff, rebase onto current main, and land after the exact head passes relevant checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history spans the internal hook architecture, bootstrap hook path, and guarded workspace reader affected by the decision.
